Changelog

LaMa (development version)

New features

  • statedens() builds the matrix of state-dependent densities of one data stream for allprobs, with parameters given per state, for all states or per observation and state; missing observations are handled for each stream separately, and log = TRUE gives log-densities for forward(…, logspace = TRUE); pseudo_res(mod) works with it

  • forward() without AD gives an error for negative allprobs, suggesting logspace = TRUE

  • forward(delta = “stationary”) computes the initial distribution from Gamma: the stationary distribution (per track if track-specific, of the first slice of each track if time-varying) or, with tod, the periodically stationary distribution at the first time point of each track

  • plot(mod, type = “statedens”) shows the state-dependent densities of each data stream built with statedens() on a histogram, weighted by the local state probabilities (or decoded states, the stationary distribution or given weights), which also works with covariates, several tracks and inhomogeneous models; the weighted densities are returned invisibly

  • plot(mod, stream = …) selects data streams, for residuals and state-dependent densities

  • simulate(mod) simulates states and observations of models built with statedens() on the observed design: same tracks and lengths, with delta, Gamma and the parameters as reported (conditional on the covariates, for continuous-time models on the observed time points); missing observations stay missing unless fill_na = TRUE, and rdens gives random number generators for densities without a matching r-function; a data stream that is NA throughout is a placeholder, so a likelihood function can be used to simulate data and then be fitted to them

  • simulate(mod, random = TRUE) and obj$simulate() of RTMB work with forward() and statedens(): statedens() registers its data like OBS(x), so random effects (with their density evaluated first, e.g. u %~% dnorm(…)) are drawn first, then the states and data given them; forward() reports the simulated states as states

  • print() and summary() for models from lama() and qreml(): print() gives a short overview, summary() the estimated state process (transition probability or generator matrix, stationary distribution and mean dwell times, averaged over tracks if track-specific) and the reported quantities, with those of length nStates in one table; summary.qremlModel() adds the smooth terms and returns an object now

  • qreml() models have class c(“qremlModel”, “LaMaModel”), so all LaMaModel methods apply to them

  • forward() reports type “track-specific” for one Gamma per track (before “homogeneous”)

  • multistart(obj) optimises an RTMB object from several starting values (obj$par and perturbations of it, or of the first fit scaled by the unit information with scale = “unit_info”), stops by a Bayesian stopping rule or once the best optimum is reached often enough, and returns the best fit with a table of all runs; lama(obj) then builds the model from the best fit

  • modmat() returns sp0, initial penalty strengths from mgcv::initial.sp() (times 100, capped at 1e6), one per penalty matrix and named as S; rep_sp() repeats them as lambda for smooths used more than once, e.g. one per state

  • print() for objects from modmat() shows the formulas and the initial penalty strengths

  • smoothdens() builds the objects for smooth (P-spline) densities from a data vector, or one object per stream from a data frame or list; density(beta) in the returned object gives the allprobs matrix and predict() the estimated densities, e.g. on the grid xseq

Changes

  • make_matrices() is renamed to modmat(); make_matrices() still works

  • report() is renamed to lama(), as it does much more than calling obj$report(); report() still works but is deprecated

  • old functions still work but are deprecated, with a message pointing to the new implementation: forward_s() and forward_sp() (use forward_hsmm() and forward_phsmm()), tpm_hsmm2() and tpm_phsmm2() (use tpm_hsmm() and tpm_phsmm()), tpm_g2() (use tpm()), qreml_old() (use qreml()), stationary_cont() and tpm_cont() (use stationary_ct() and tpm_ct())

  • deprecation messages are shown once per session, not at every call

  • lama(): the log-likelihood is called llk (before ll), as for qreml()

  • lama() and qreml(): nobs does not count missing observations (rows of allprobs that are all 1), which changes BIC for data with missing observations

  • lama() stores the maximum gradient component mgc to check convergence

  • pseudo_res(mod) computes pseudo-residuals from the model object alone: the likelihood function is evaluated again with its densities replaced by their CDFs, after checking that this is valid; several data streams give one set of residuals each; also for qreml() models and densities in helper functions

  • scores(mod) computes the score contribution of each observation for models using forward(), e.g. for robust (sandwich) standard errors; it takes the model from lama() or the RTMB object, respects map, and the likelihood function does not need to change

  • lama() also stores obj (the same object, not a copy), so MCreport() can be called on the model object from lama() or qreml()

  • pred_matrix() is deprecated, use predict() on the object from modmat() instead

  • make_matrices_old() is removed

  • smooth_dens_construct() is deprecated, use smoothdens() instead

  • make_matrices_dens() and smooth_dens_construct() no longer print messages; basis$knots includes the boundary knots

Bug fixes

  • Examples and vignettes: the periodically stationary initial distribution matches forward()’s tod, where Gamma[,,tod[t]] is the transition into t, i.e. stationary_p(Gamma, tod[1] %% L + 1)

  • lama(): the log-likelihood was evaluated at the last parameters the optimiser tried, not the best

  • summary.qremlModel() failed for reported lists or character vectors, and if Gamma was not reported but delta was

  • pseudo_res(): missing observations give NA in all variants (before 0 with normal = FALSE, -Inf for non-randomised discrete residuals)

  • pseudo_res(): parameters given per observation (matrix or vector of length nObs) work with missing observations

  • forward(): with track-specific delta or Gamma, the AD version matched them to the wrong tracks if the track IDs were not sorted (e.g. “ID1”, …, “ID10”)

  • forward(): tracks of length one failed with AD

  • logspace = TRUE is now exact (delta is no longer modified) and also stable without AD

  • one-state models are correct with logspace = TRUE and report their quantities

  • forward_p() works if tod does not contain all values 1, …, L

  • forward_g() works without AD for two observations

  • stateprobs_g(forecast = TRUE) with trackID used the transition matrix of the previous time point, which also affected pseudo_res() for inhomogeneous models with tracks

  • stateprobs() passes forecast on for time-varying Gamma

  • viterbi() and stateprobs() work for tracks of length one

  • stateprobs(forecast = TRUE): the first row of each track is delta, not the filtered probabilities given x_1, so pseudo_res() is correct for the first observation

  • modmat(): smooths with several penalties but not one per margin (e.g. bs = “fs”, “ad” or t2(full = TRUE)) kept only the first, so later smooths got the wrong penalty matrices

  • modmat(): a nested formula list failed if one data stream had no smooth terms

  • modmat(): tensor product margins over several covariates are named e.g. “x,y” (two such margins failed); unpenalised smooths (fx = TRUE) give an informative error

  • predict() on objects from modmat() ignored exclude

  • smooth_dens_construct(): coefficients of one state are a matrix (before a vector, so cbind(coef, 0) was wrong); circular data with custom knots failed; angles outside [-pi, pi) are wrapped; par accepts kappa next to concentration

  • make_matrices_dens(): the basis is normalised on a midpoint grid (before a fixed 1e-3 offset, which gave negative weights for data on a small scale), which changes the weights very slightly

Minor changes

  • forward(), forward_g() and forward_p() share one implementation (one C++ and one R version for AD); forward_p() no longer expands Gamma for the computation
  • tracks need to be contiguous, otherwise forward() gives an informative error
  • without AD, forward() gives an error for NA in allprobs
  • the TapeConfig performance tip is shown only once per session
  • viterbi(), stateprobs() and their _g and _p versions use the inputs of forward() and one C++ implementation each, so Gamma is no longer expanded; as in forward(), tracks need to be contiguous
  • forward_p() reports Gamma with its L slices and type “periodic”
  • forward(), viterbi() and stateprobs() have an argument tod for periodic models, so they handle all model types; forward_g(), forward_p(), viterbi_g(), viterbi_p(), stateprobs_g() and stateprobs_p() are deprecated and give a message
  • viterbi() and stateprobs() also take the model object as first argument, e.g. viterbi(mod) instead of viterbi(mod = mod)
  • tpm_g() and generator_g() are deprecated in favour of tpm(beta, Z) and generator(beta, Z), which also accept a single covariate vector Z; the sparse argument of tpm_g() is gone
  • modmat() sets up each basis once and no longer keeps gam$X (returned as Z), so it is faster and needs less memory

LaMa 2.1.1 (2026-05-13)

CRAN release: 2026-05-13

Major changes

  • vignettes 1-3 have been updated to work with automatic differentiation

  • tpm(), forward(), stateprobs(), viterbi() can now be used with inhomogeneous models: call their inhomogeneous counterparts internally

  • function MCreport() has been added for sampling

    • from the distribution of the MLE (fixed effects only models)
    • from the joint post. distribution of parameters and random effects (random effects models)

Minor changes

  • some functions have been renamed, e.g. stationary_cont() -> stationary_ct() (old versions still exist)

  • some internal cleanup
